notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My research tool stopped working before any page loaded, so I have no sources for Ezekiel 29.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word's chapter page, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com, Precept Austin's commentary page, and the NET Bible notes. The tool reported I had used up my allowed calls before it returned anything, and I have no other way to reach the web.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without any pages, anything I wrote would come from memory with no source behind it. So I've left everything out rather than give you notes that only look sourced.

**Next step:** Ask me again in a new message and I'll start the research from scratch. I'll make the calls more slowly and in smaller groups so the limit doesn't stop me again. I'd begin with:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word's Ezekiel 29 page and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit commentaries on biblehub.com or studylight.org.
2. **Protestant differences:** I'd look for real disagreements, most likely over the "forty years" in vv. 11–13, God paying Nebuchadnezzar for Tyre in vv. 17–20, and the "horn" in v. 21 (whether it points to the Messiah). I'd check sources such as wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), spurgeon.org, gty.org and ligonier.org.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox sites, including commentary on Tyre not being taken in v. 18.
